hints: Look closely at the thickness of each block, not just the length. Which block has the shortest distance from the outside to the very centre for the acid to travel?
Remember that diffusion speed depends on surface area to volume ratio. Think about how to calculate SA:V for a cuboid with $SA = 2(lw + lh + wh)$ and which size gives the largest ratio.
walkthrough:
**Understand what fastest means**

Think like the acid. To change the whole block, it must diffuse from the surface to the centre.

A larger surface area to volume ratio means more entry surface per unit of agar to fill, plus a shorter diffusion distance, so colour change is faster.

**Calculate surface area to volume ratio**

Use for a cuboid:
$$SA = 2(lw + lh + wh)$$
$$V = l \times w \times h$$
$$Ratio = SA \div V$$

For example, for B:
$$SA = 2(1 \times 0.25 + 1 \times 0.25 + 0.25 \times 0.25) = 1.125 \text{ mm}^2$$
$$V = 1 \times 0.25 \times 0.25 = 0.0625 \text{ mm}^3$$
$$Ratio = 1.125 \div 0.0625 = 18 \text{ mm}^{-1}$$

**Compare and conclude**

Doing the same gives A = $6 \text{ mm}^{-1}$, C = $10 \text{ mm}^{-1}$, D = $9 \text{ mm}^{-1}$.

Block B is the smallest and thinnest, so it has the largest SA:V of $18 \text{ mm}^{-1}$ and the shortest diffusion path. It will be penetrated completely the fastest.

options.A: This is a $1 \text{ mm}$ cube with SA:V of only $6 \text{ mm}^{-1}$. It has the largest volume to fill, so it is the slowest.
options.B: This is the smallest block with the largest SA:V of $18 \text{ mm}^{-1}$ and only $0.125 \text{ mm}$ to the centre, so acid reaches everywhere fastest.
options.C: Its SA:V is $10 \text{ mm}^{-1}$, which is faster than A and D but still much lower than B because it is thicker than B.
options.D: Although thin, it is twice as long as C, giving a larger volume and a lower SA:V of $9 \text{ mm}^{-1}$, so it is slower than B and C.
